D019-D020_h001.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time since that car accident a little while ago. I’m still going into the office a few days a week and working from home the rest, but I feel like I’m running on empty all the time. I technically sleep 7–8 hours most nights, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t slept at all. It’s like my body rests but my brain doesn’t. By mid-afternoon my eyes burn at the screen, and I’m rereading the same lines of code over and over.

What’s freaking me out the most are these moments where it feels like I’m back on the highway. It’s not just remembering it—I’ll hear brakes outside or see a sudden movement in my peripheral vision, and for a few seconds it’s like I’m right there again, waiting for the impact. My heart jumps, I lose track of what I’m doing, and then I sort of “snap” back to my desk or my apartment.

This has been going on for a bit now. I’m still doing my job, but slower, and I’m avoiding driving whenever I can. I feel worn down and not like myself.
D019-D020_h001.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h001.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h002.question:
It’s been…honestly, I’m not even sure how long anymore, just “since everything happened” with my son’s accident and the layoffs at my firm. The days blur together. I’m still going to work, still doing people’s taxes and audits, but I feel like I’m moving on autopilot.

Nights are the worst. I fall asleep easily enough because I’m exhausted, but then I’m awake at 2 or 3 a.m., heart pounding, staring at the ceiling. I’ll doze off and then wake again, over and over. When I do sleep, I keep having these awful dreams—sometimes it’s the phone ringing in the middle of the night like when they called about my son, sometimes I’m driving and can’t hit the brakes in time. I wake up sweaty, with this heavy feeling in my chest, and it’s hard to settle back down.

I don’t know if this is just a reaction to everything or something more serious, but I can’t seem to shake it, and it’s starting to wear me out. My husband says I’m more irritable and distracted, even when we’re just doing normal things at home.
D019-D020_h002.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h002.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h003.question:
It’s been…a little while now since that house job where the ceiling collapsed. I don’t even know exactly how long, just “since then.” Nobody got seriously hurt, but it shook me up more than I expected.

Since that day, my sleep’s been off. I’m technically getting six, seven hours, but I wake up feeling like I’ve barely slept. My body’s sore, my head’s heavy, and I’m dragging through the day. My wife says I’m snoring the same as always, but I don’t feel rested at all, even on nights I’m in bed early.

What really bothers me is how I react to certain things now. If I’m under a house or in a tight crawlspace and I hear wood creak, or if I see dust falling from a ceiling, my chest tightens and my heart starts racing. Even just driving past that street or hearing a noise that sounds like something giving way, I get this jolt, like I’m right back there for a second. Sometimes it fades quick, sometimes it hangs around and I can’t shake it, and it makes it harder to focus on the work in front of me.
D019-D020_h003.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h003.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h004.question:
It’s been… I don’t even know, a couple of weeks maybe? Time’s kind of blurry since the accident at the warehouse. I keep telling myself it wasn’t that bad, nobody died, but it’s stuck in my head.

Nights are the worst. I’ll get into bed at like 11, exhausted, but then I’m just lying there, staring at the ceiling for what feels like hours. My mind keeps replaying the sound of the crates crashing, the yelling, thinking someone was pinned. Even if I try to think about something else, it circles back to that moment. I eventually fall asleep, but it takes a long time, and I dread going to bed now.

At work, if I hear a loud bang from the loading dock or see a pallet wobble even a little, my chest tightens. I get this rush of panic, like it’s happening again, and I have to look away or step outside for a minute. Even driving past the warehouse on my day off makes me feel on edge. I know it probably seems minor to other people, but I just can’t seem to shake it.
D019-D020_h004.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h004.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h005.question:
I’ve been having a really hard time since…well, since that incident at work a little while ago. I don’t even know exactly when it started, it just sort of crept in afterward.

Most nights I fall asleep exhausted, but I keep waking up around four in the morning, wide awake, heart racing, and I just lie there replaying everything. I can’t get back to sleep, and then I still have to be on air at six, smiling like nothing’s wrong.

What’s bothering me most is how jumpy and on edge I feel whenever anything reminds me of that night. If I hear a similar sound in the studio, or see a clip that even vaguely resembles it in the newsroom, I get this wave of panic and my chest tightens. Even just thinking about it when I’m putting on my makeup before the show can set me off. Sometimes it’s a word in the teleprompter or a piece of breaking news that has a similar tone, and I feel my throat close up and I have to push the feeling down to keep reading.

It’s not constant, but it’s frequent enough that it’s starting to interfere with how I function, both on camera and at home.
D019-D020_h005.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
D019-D020_h005.answer: C & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h006.question:
I work nights doing lights for concerts, so I’m used to weird sleep, but this is different. For the past week or so—honestly I’m not sure exactly how long—I keep waking up way before my alarm, like 4 a.m., and then I just lie there, wide awake. My body feels tired, but my brain won’t shut off, and I can’t fall back asleep.

It started after that incident at the venue. I can picture certain parts in sharp detail—the sound, the way everyone suddenly moved—but other parts are just… blank. People ask me what happened in between and I sort of freeze, because I don’t actually remember those bits, like there’s a gap in the middle of the whole thing.

What’s bothering me most is I feel flat. Normally I get a kick out of pulling off a tricky lighting cue or seeing the crowd react when everything hits just right. Lately, even when a show goes perfectly or my friends try to cheer me up, it’s like nothing lands. I can see that it should feel good, but there’s no actual sense of happiness, just this numb, muted feeling.
D019-D020_h006.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h006.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h007.question:
It’s been… I’m not even sure how long, a few weeks maybe, since that incident at work. I keep calling it “the incident” because I honestly can’t remember most of what actually happened. I know there was an accident at the transfer station, alarms, people shouting, and then it’s just bits and pieces—someone on the ground, flashing lights—and then nothing. My coworkers will tell me details and it’s like they’re talking about a movie I must’ve seen, not something I was there for.

What’s really getting to me now is the nights. I wake up sweating from these horrible dreams. I can’t even say exactly what I see, but I wake up with my heart racing and this feeling like something terrible just happened all over again. My wife says I thrash around and sometimes shout, but I rarely remember the dream clearly—just the panic.

During the day I still go to work, I do my job, meet the targets. But even when something goes well—a route gets optimized, complaints go down—I feel nothing. No sense of “well done,” no pride. It’s like I’m just going through the motions, and whatever used to feel satisfying about my work, or even stuff at home, just doesn’t land anymore.
D019-D020_h007.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h007.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h008.question:
It started after that really rough flight a little while ago. We hit unexpected turbulence on a night route, passengers were screaming, the masks dropped, and for a few minutes I honestly thought we were going down. Since then, my sleep’s been a mess. When I do manage to sleep, I keep getting these really vivid, horrible dreams about being back on the plane. Sometimes it’s exactly what happened, sometimes it’s twisted, but I wake up with my heart racing and I can’t get back to sleep.

What’s weird is my memory of the actual incident feels patchy. I remember some parts in sharp detail—like one woman’s face and the sound of the overhead bins slamming—but other bits are just… blank. My husband asks me to walk him through it, and there are sections I just can’t seem to bring up, like the time right before and right after the worst of it.

During the day, especially when I’m not on a flight, I feel kind of shut down emotionally. It’s like I’m going through the motions—talking to passengers, chatting with my husband—but I feel empty inside, like someone turned the volume down on all my feelings, even the good ones. I’m not sure how long this is supposed to last or if it’s just me not coping well with what happened.
D019-D020_h008.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h008.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h009.question:
I guess the whole thing really started sometime after that outage at work a while back. It was a mess—clients yelling, senior leadership on calls all night, everyone blaming everyone. I keep thinking about it, but it’s weird: I remember very specific parts, like the error messages on the dashboard and my manager’s voice on speaker, but other chunks are just… blank. People mention things I supposedly said or did during that call, and I can’t picture them at all.

Since then my sleep’s gone off the rails. When I finally crash, I can sleep 10–12 hours straight and still wake up heavy, like I could go right back to bed. On weekends I end up napping half the afternoon without really meaning to. It’s not exactly insomnia—I’m almost sleeping too much.

What bothers me is that nothing feels rewarding. I pushed a big redesign to production last week, something I’d been working toward for months, and everyone said it was a win. I just felt… flat. No sense of “I did it,” no pride, just moving to the next ticket in the queue. I’m functioning, but it all feels kind of hollow.
D019-D020_h009.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h009.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h010.question:
I’m not even sure where to start. Ever since…well, since the incident at the library a little while back, I’ve felt like I’m watching my own life from somewhere else. I know something awful happened — the police came, there were paramedics — but when I try to play it back in my mind, it’s like the film just cuts out. I remember little flashes, but most of it is just…blank.

What I notice most is the mornings. I wake up around four, sometimes earlier, and that’s it — I’m wide awake, and there’s no getting back to sleep. My mind starts turning over things, but not in a clear way. I just lie there waiting for the alarm, feeling tired and strangely empty.

My sister keeps checking on me, and my staff at the library have been very kind, but I feel oddly detached from all of them. I know, intellectually, that I care about them, but I don’t feel it in my chest the way I used to. When they hug me or tell me they’re worried, it barely registers. It’s like the part of me that can really love people has gone quiet.
D019-D020_h010.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D019-D020_h010.answer: B & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h011.question:
I’ve been out here on my own for a while, and lately I feel… off. I can’t seem to make simple choices anymore. In the mornings I’ll just stand there, staring at my two work jackets, unable to decide which one to put on. Same with what to eat, or whether to fix something now or later. I end up pacing back and forth over really small things.

I’ve also gotten into this habit of checking things over and over. Before I go up the tower, I walk the perimeter, make sure every door is locked, then go back and check again, sometimes a third time. When I’m in town for supplies, I keep scanning the room, watching who comes in and where the exits are. It doesn’t feel voluntary; it’s like I can’t relax unless I do it.

And if someone touches me unexpectedly—like when the supply guy clapped me on the shoulder last trip—I jump out of my skin. It’s embarrassing; my whole body jerks and my heart starts racing. I don’t know exactly when this all started, but it’s been recent enough that I still remember what it was like to feel normal.
D019-D020_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h011.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h012.question:
I’m not really sure when all this started…maybe a couple of weeks, maybe less. Time’s been kind of fuzzy since everything went sideways with the farm this season. Prices dropped, the storms ruined a good chunk of the crop, and we’ve been worried about money. I keep telling myself other years were bad too, but this feels different.

Lately I can’t seem to switch off. Even when I’m in the house at night, doors locked, sitting in my own chair, it’s like my body’s still out in the field waiting for something to go wrong. My shoulders are tight all the time, and I’m constantly listening for… I don’t even know what. Any small noise makes me jump. If my wife drops a pot in the kitchen or a truck backfires on the road, I flinch like someone’s come up behind me.

I also can’t make simple choices anymore. My wife asks what I want for supper and I just stare at her, going back and forth over something that used to be nothing. Same with which field to start with, or even what shirt to put on. I hesitate and second-guess everything, and it’s wearing me out.
D019-D020_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h012.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h013.question:
It’s been…honestly I’m not even sure how long, a little while since everything happened at the restaurant, but lately I just don’t feel like myself.

My head feels foggy a lot of the time, like I’m half there and half not. I’ll be going over the orders or the staff schedule and suddenly I can’t think straight, like my brain just stalls. I find myself zoning out in the middle of conversations with my cooks or my husband and then I realize I missed half of what they said.

I’m constantly on edge at the restaurant now. I keep checking the entrance, the windows, the parking lot. Even when I’m talking to a customer, part of me is watching who’s coming in, what people are doing with their hands, if anyone looks off. It’s like I’m waiting for something bad to happen again, even if nothing’s going on.

And if someone comes around a corner too fast in the kitchen, or a server suddenly appears behind me, I jump. Same if a shadow moves in my peripheral vision. I whip around like I’m bracing for something, even when it’s just one of my staff or my kids at home. It’s embarrassing, and I can’t seem to switch it off.
D019-D020_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h013.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h014.question:
I’m not really sure how to explain it, but since the break‑in at the community center a little while ago, I just haven’t felt like myself. My head feels…foggy, like I’m moving through cotton. I’ll be in the middle of sorting donations and suddenly lose my train of thought, or I’ll just stare at a form and can’t seem to process the words. It comes and goes, but it’s been happening often enough that I’ve started to worry.

When I’m at the center, I catch myself looking around a lot. I notice where the exits are, who’s coming in and out, whether the back door is really locked. I’ll check the door, walk away, and then go back again because I’m not sure I did it properly. Even walking to my car, I keep glancing over my shoulder.

I’ve also become very jumpy. If someone brushes past me from behind or puts a hand on my shoulder without warning, my whole body jerks and my heart races. It’s embarrassing—I know it’s just one of the other volunteers, but my reaction feels way out of proportion.
D019-D020_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h014.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h015.question:
It’s been… I don’t even really know, a little while since that bad call at work, but not that long. Days? Maybe a bit more. Time’s kind of blurry. Since then, I just feel “off.” It’s like my head’s full of cotton. On scene or even just at home, I’ll kind of drift out for a second, like I’m there but not really thinking straight. Simple stuff that I normally do automatically, I have to double‑check because I don’t trust my own brain.

I’ve also been really jumpy. If a door slams at the station or someone drops a metal tray, I flinch hard, like my whole body jerks before I even realize what happened. The guys have joked about it, but it doesn’t feel funny to me.

I keep scanning rooms without meaning to. When I walk into a store, I’m noting the exits, the people, who’s near the door. Even at home I’ll recheck that the door’s locked or look out the window to see who’s around. I know nothing’s actually happening, but I just don’t feel fully settled or clear in my head.
D019-D020_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h015.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h016.question:
It’s been…honestly, I’m not even sure how long anymore, a little while since the accident, but the days all blur together.

I keep getting these flashes in my head when I’m driving between client meetings or even just sitting at my desk—bits and pieces of that day. It’s like a movie clip that just jumps in without warning: the screeching sound, a glimpse of shattered glass, my heart pounding. I don’t sit there trying to think about it; it just crashes in on its own, and I’m right back there for a second.

At the same time, there’s this big blank spot. I can’t really piece together what happened from start to finish. My wife keeps asking what exactly went on, and I honestly don’t know. I remember leaving a client’s office, then…fragments. People have filled in details, but in my own head it’s mostly just missing.

I’m doing a lot to not stir it up. I reroute my drives to avoid that stretch of road, make excuses to skip in‑person meetings near that area, and if colleagues or my wife bring it up, I shut it down or change the subject because it makes my chest tighten.
D019-D020_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h016.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h017.question:
It’s hard to explain because parts of it are just…blank. I know something bad happened a little while ago, but I can’t really piece it together. It’s like the whole thing is behind a fog. I remember bits—sirens, people shouting—but most of it is just gone, and when I try to think about it, my mind kind of slams a door shut.

When anything reminds me of it—like a certain ringtone, or even driving past that general area—I feel my heart start pounding out of nowhere. I get sweaty, my chest tightens, and sometimes my hands shake so much I have to pull over. Even sitting at my desk at the agency, if a client starts talking about accidents or claims that sound even vaguely similar, I feel this wave of dizziness and nausea.

Because of that, I do everything I can not to think about it. I change the subject, leave the room, keep myself busy with paperwork. At night, if my mind starts drifting there, I’ll scroll on my phone or turn on the TV just to drown it out. I don’t know exactly how long this has been going on—weeks, maybe—but it’s long enough that it’s starting to wear me down.
D019-D020_h017.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h017.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h018.question:
I’ve been driving trains for about ten years, so I’m used to weird shifts and being tired, but this feels different. Since that incident on the platform a little while ago, my sleep’s been a mess. When I do sleep, I get these really vivid dreams that feel tied to what happened—lots of noise, brakes screeching, people shouting—but it’s all jumbled. I wake up sweating and anxious, heart racing.

What’s strange is I can’t actually remember the whole thing clearly. It’s like my mind has cut out chunks of it. I remember coming into the station and then… just flashes. Sirens, someone grabbing my arm, my supervisor talking to me. If I try to really think it through, my head kind of shuts down; I just push it away.

At work, I keep telling dispatch I’m fine, but I dread that particular station. If I can swap runs to avoid it, I do. Even off duty, I catch myself changing the channel if there’s anything about accidents or the subway. I don’t really talk about it with my coworkers or my family—every time I start, I feel this wave of panic, so I just say, “It’s nothing, I’m over it,” and change the subject.
D019-D020_h018.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h018.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h019.question:
I’m still trying to piece together what actually happened that night. People keep asking for details, and it’s like my brain just hits a wall. I remember flashes—sirens, people yelling—but most of it is just…blank. I’ve sold houses on that street for years, so it’s strange that I can’t replay it in my head the way I normally can with events. It’s been…a little while now, but I honestly couldn’t tell you exactly how long. The days are kind of running together.

When anything reminds me of it—a certain car horn, the smell of asphalt after rain, driving past that intersection—I feel my heart start racing, my hands sweat, my chest gets tight, like I might pass out. Even my own thoughts set it off; if my mind starts drifting toward that night, I snap the radio on, call a client, scroll my phone—anything to shut it down. I’ve started rerouting my showings so I don’t have to go near that block, telling myself it’s just “traffic” or “construction,” but really I’m just trying not to think about it at all.
D019-D020_h019.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h019.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h020.question:
It started after that night with the car accident a little while ago… I’m not even sure exactly how long it’s been now, a few weeks maybe? Time’s kind of blurry. Since then, it’s like pieces of it just pop into my head when I’m not expecting it. I’ll be loading the dishwasher or helping my daughter with homework and suddenly I’m right back there—hearing the screech, seeing the lights. I don’t choose to think about it; it just forces its way in and my whole body tenses.

At the same time, there are gaps. I can picture the moment right before the impact and then flashes from the hospital, but I can’t seem to fill in what happened in between. My husband tried asking me to go over it with the insurance people and I honestly can’t recall certain parts, no matter how hard I try.

I catch myself doing everything I can not to think about it. I avoid the route where it happened, I turn off movies with crashes, and if my mind even starts to go near that night, I force myself to focus on something else—housework, the kids—anything but that.
D019-D020_h020.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D019-D020_h020.answer: A & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h021.question:
It started after that accident at the shop a little while back—time’s kind of a blur, maybe weeks, maybe less, I’m not really sure. One of the lifts slipped and a car came down harder than it should have. Nobody died, but for a second I thought my coworker was gone. Since then, it’s like my head keeps replaying it on its own.

I’ll be working on a transmission or just sitting at dinner with my wife and kids, and suddenly I see it again—the car dropping, the sound, him yelling. It’s not like I’m trying to think about it; it just jumps in. Sometimes I flinch when I hear a loud bang in the shop and my mind goes right back there.

I’ve been snapping at people a lot more. At work, if someone makes a small mistake, I bark at them, swear, tell them they’re going to get someone killed. At home, my wife will ask a simple question and I’ll blow up, raise my voice, say things I don’t mean. Then I feel bad afterward, but in the moment I can’t seem to hold it back.
D019-D020_h021.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h021.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h022.question:
It started after everything blew up with my ex and the divorce got really ugly. I don’t even know exactly when it crossed from “normal stress” into…whatever this is, but it’s been going on for a little while now.

I’ll be at the studio, trying to cue someone through breathing, and then a song we used to play at home comes on, or I see a text from my lawyer, and my whole body just tightens. It feels like I’m back in the middle of one of our fights. My chest squeezes, my mind races, and I just want to run out of the room. Sometimes it’s just a random thought about court or money and I’m instantly on edge, like my brain won’t let it go.

I’ve also been snapping at people in a way that’s not like me. If a client is late or cancels, I’ll just unload on them or on the receptionist—raising my voice, saying things I regret right after. I even yelled at my sister on the phone over something tiny. I can tell I’m overreacting, but in the moment it feels like everything is someone else’s fault and I can’t hold it in.
D019-D020_h022.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h022.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h023.question:
Honestly, I don’t even know how to explain what’s been going on. There was this case a little while back in the trauma bay that went really bad, and ever since then things have felt…off. Time-wise, I’m not exactly sure when it started, it just kind of bled into everything.

Sometimes I’ll be in the OR or even just walking down the hall, and for a few seconds it feels like I’m right back in that room with that patient. It’s not just remembering it—my chest tightens, the sounds get weirdly loud, and I almost forget where I actually am. Then it passes and I’m embarrassed, hoping no one noticed I zoned out.

Outside of that, I’m on edge all the time. Little things set me off—someone being slow with a chart, a nurse asking a routine question. I snap or get really short, then feel guilty afterward. I’m not sleeping great, but I’m still making it through call. I’ve been trying to just push through and focus on work, but it feels like my fuse is a lot shorter than it used to be, and those “replay” moments are starting to bother me.

D019-D020_h024.question:
It’s been…honestly, I’ve lost track, maybe a few weeks? A bit more? Since my wife passed, everything’s felt off. Most of the time I’m quiet, but then something small sets me off and I turn into someone I don’t recognize.

For example, the other day my daughter dropped off one of my wife’s scarves. As soon as I smelled her perfume on it, my chest tightened, my heart started pounding, and I just felt like I couldn’t breathe. I got so wound up I ended up slamming a chair into the table and cracked one of the kitchen tiles. Another time, when my grandson accidentally played one of the old songs from our wedding, I just snapped and shoved the stereo off the shelf. I didn’t hurt him, but I yelled, and the look on his face… I’m ashamed of that.

Anything that reminds me of her—certain smells, her favorite TV shows, even walking past our bedroom—can send me into this overwhelming wave of upset. I go from numb to furious in seconds, and afterward I feel exhausted and guilty, but I can’t seem to stop it when it happens.
D019-D020_h024.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h024.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder

D019-D020_h025.question:
It’s been…a few weeks? Maybe more. Time’s a bit of a blur since everything happened with the firm and the case blowing up in the press. I’m still going into the office, but I feel like I’m walking around with my teeth permanently clenched.

Little things set me off. An associate asking a basic question, my ex texting about our son’s tuition—my temper just snaps. I’m not yelling at people constantly, but I can feel it right under the surface all the time, like I’m about to bite someone’s head off. I’m not usually like that; I’m used to pressure.

What really scares me is how my body reacts. If I hear a certain news clip about the case, or someone mentions that client’s name, my heart starts pounding, my hands shake, I get this tightness in my chest, like I’ve had five cups of coffee on an empty stomach. Even driving past the courthouse, I sometimes break out in a sweat and feel almost lightheaded. I keep telling myself it’s just stress, that I should be able to manage it, but it doesn’t seem to be settling down, and it’s starting to interfere with how I work and how I deal with people.

A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Adjustment Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D020_h025.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Adjustment Disorder
